sop_modules.name: Trim Stain/Clear Setup
sop_modules.description: Floor protection and wall/fixture masking for trim stain and clear coat work. Protection scope varies by application method and adjacent wall state.

tasks.name: Floor Protection Setup (Perimeter Drops)
tasks.description: Set up drop cloth runners along trim work area perimeter. Stain drips are especially difficult to clean — protection is critical.

quality_notes.all: Runner-style drops along baseboard and trim run areas. Stain drips penetrate — canvas drops preferred over plastic.

tasks.name: Wall Masking at Trim Edge
tasks.description: Apply tape line and masking paper at trim-to-wall edge. Required for spray. Also required for any method when walls are SS_PAINTED_* — stain penetrates and cannot be wiped off painted surfaces.

quality_notes.all: Complete tape line along trim-to-wall edge. Paper drape for spray.

tasks.name: Cover Fixtures Near Spray Zone
tasks.description: Tape over outlets and switches near spray work area.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of outlet/switch plates near spray zone.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Floor protection first, then wall masking (if applicable), then fixture covers (if spray).

sop_modules.name: Bare Wood Preparation
sop_modules.description: Prepare bare wood trim for staining. Sand to profile (120 then 150 grit), fill defects with stainable wood filler, grain raise treatment (conditional for waterborne products), tack clean.

tasks.name: Inspect Bare Wood
tasks.description: Visual inspection of bare wood trim surfaces. Check for mill marks, dents, nail holes, wood defects, and grain pattern consistency.

quality_notes.QT3: Quick scan — note obvious defects, deep mill marks, open nail holes
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic inspection — mark all visible defects, check grain consistency
quality_notes.QT5: Thorough inspection under raking light — mark every imperfection that could show through stain

tasks.name: Sand Bare Wood (120 Grit)
tasks.description: Initial sanding with 120-grit to remove mill marks, raised grain, and surface imperfections. Sand WITH the grain direction.

quality_notes.all: Sand with grain direction only. Remove all mill marks. Uniform scratch pattern. Do NOT cross-grain sand — scratches will show through stain.

tasks.name: Sand Bare Wood (150 Grit)
tasks.description: Final prep sanding with 150-grit for smooth stain-ready surface. Removes 120-grit scratch pattern.

quality_notes.all: Uniform 150-grit scratch pattern with grain. Surface should feel smooth to touch. No visible 120-grit scratches remaining.

tasks.name: Fill Defects (Stainable Wood Filler)
tasks.description: Fill nail holes, dents, and defects with stainable wood filler. NOT regular spackle — spackle does not accept stain.

quality_notes.QT3: Fill open nail holes and obvious dents
quality_notes.QT4: Fill all visible defects — nail holes, dents, small cracks
quality_notes.QT5: Fill every defect that could show through stain. Color-match filler to expected stain color.

tasks.name: Grain Raise Treatment (Waterborne)
tasks.description: Wet-wipe bare wood to intentionally raise grain, let dry, re-sand with 220 grit. Prevents grain raise from first waterborne product application.

applies_when._note: Activated when ANY waterborne product is selected (WB stain, WB sealer, or WB clear) and no oil-based product precedes it in the stack

quality_notes.all: Wet wipe entire surface with damp sponge. Let dry completely (1-2 hrs). Re-sand with 220 grit to knock down raised fibers. Tack clean after.

tasks.name: Tack Clean (Prep Complete)
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust from trim surfaces with tack cloth. Surface must be perfectly clean before stain or conditioner application.

quality_notes.all: All dust removed — surface clean to touch. Dust in stain creates visible defects that cannot be sanded out.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect → Sand 120 → Sand 150 → Fill Defects → Grain Raise (conditional) → Tack Clean. All prep complete before conditioner or stain.

sop_modules.name: Wood Conditioner Application
sop_modules.description: Apply pre-stain wood conditioner to softwood trim to prevent blotchy stain absorption. Conditional: softwood + stain coating_type + NOT gel stain.

applies_when._note: NOT activated when gel stain selected — gel controls blotch inherently

tasks.name: Apply Wood Conditioner
tasks.description: Brush on pre-stain wood conditioner liberally. Let penetrate per manufacturer instructions (~15 min).

quality_notes.all: Apply liberally, ensure full coverage. Let dwell 15 minutes per manufacturer instructions.

tasks.name: Wipe Excess Conditioner
tasks.description: Wipe off excess conditioner with clean lint-free cloth. Stain must be applied within 2 hours of conditioner.

quality_notes.all: Wipe off all excess. Surface should feel slightly tacky, not wet. Apply stain within 2 hours.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Apply conditioner → Wait 15 min → Wipe excess → Apply stain within 2 hours.

sop_modules.name: Stain Application (Coat 1)
sop_modules.description: Apply first stain coat. All methods include a wipe step to control color depth and uniformity. Brush+wipe, roll+wipe, or spray+wipe.

tasks.name: Stain Coat 1 — Brush + Wipe
tasks.description: Apply stain with brush, working with the grain. Maintain wet edge. After appropriate dwell time, wipe excess with lint-free cloth to control color depth.

quality_notes.all: Apply with grain. Maintain wet edge — lap marks in stain are permanent. Wipe evenly for uniform color. Application quality is NOT tiered.

tasks.name: Stain Coat 1 — Roll + Wipe
tasks.description: Apply stain with foam mini roller, working with the grain. After dwell time, wipe excess with lint-free cloth.

quality_notes.all: Use foam roller (lint-free). Roll with grain. Wipe promptly for even color. Application quality is NOT tiered.

tasks.name: Stain Coat 1 — Spray + Wipe
tasks.description: Spray stain onto trim surfaces. After dwell time, wipe excess with lint-free cloth. Back-brushing into profile details recommended.

quality_notes.all: Spray even coat. Back-brush into crevices/profiles. Wipe evenly. Application quality is NOT tiered.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Apply stain → Dwell per product instructions → Wipe excess. One method per variant.

sop_modules.name: Stain Application (Coat 2)
sop_modules.description: Apply second stain coat for deeper color saturation. Conditional: stain_coats = 2.

tasks.name: Stain Coat 2 — Apply + Wipe
tasks.description: Apply second stain coat using same method as coat 1. Wipe for color depth control. Coat 2 builds deeper color on areas that absorbed less on first coat.

quality_notes.all: Same method as coat 1. Second coat builds color where first was light. Wipe evenly. Verify color uniformity across all trim types.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Same method as coat 1. Second coat for deeper, more uniform color.

sop_modules.name: Stain Dry Verification
sop_modules.description: Verify stain is fully dry before applying sealer or clear coat. Conditional: stain applied AND clear coat follows.

tasks.name: Verify Stain Dry
tasks.description: Touch-test stain dryness. Oil stain: 4-8 hours dry time. Waterborne stain: 2 hours. Surface must be completely dry and non-tacky before sealer/clear.

quality_notes.all: Touch test in inconspicuous area. No tackiness. No color transfer to cloth. If tacky, wait longer — do NOT apply sealer/clear over tacky stain.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Wait for full dry time per product instructions, then verify.

sop_modules.name: Sanding Sealer Application (Coat 1)
sop_modules.description: Apply first coat of sanding sealer. Builds smooth base for clear topcoat. Conditional: sealer_coats >= 1.

tasks.name: Apply Sanding Sealer (Coat 1)
tasks.description: Apply thin, even coat of sanding sealer. Brush or spray per application_method_clear. Sealer builds adhesion bridge and creates sandable base.

quality_notes.all: Thin, even coat. Do not over-apply — sealer should not pool in profiles. Let dry per product instructions before sanding.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Apply sealer → Dry → Sand (in MOD_TRST_SEALER_INTERSTAGE or MOD_TRST_SEALER_SAND).

sop_modules.name: Sealer Interstage + Coat 2
sop_modules.description: Sand first sealer coat and apply second sealer coat. Conditional: sealer_coats = 2.

tasks.name: Sand Sealer (220 Grit)
tasks.description: Sand first sealer coat with 220-grit. Level surface, remove nibs and dust inclusions. Rigid sanding block for flat areas.

quality_notes.all: Sand entire surface with 220 grit. Level sealer coat. Do NOT sand through to stain — light pressure only.

tasks.name: Tack Clean Between Sealer Coats
tasks.description: Remove sanding dust with tack cloth before second sealer coat.

quality_notes.all: Complete dust removal before next coat.

tasks.name: Apply Sanding Sealer (Coat 2)
tasks.description: Apply second coat of sanding sealer over sanded first coat.

quality_notes.all: Thin, even coat. Same technique as coat 1.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Sand sealer → Tack → Apply sealer coat 2 → Dry → Final sealer sand (in MOD_TRST_SEALER_SAND).

sop_modules.name: Final Sealer Sand Before Clear
sop_modules.description: Sand final sealer coat to glass-smooth surface before first clear topcoat. Conditional: sealer_coats >= 1.

tasks.name: Final Sealer Sand (320 Grit)
tasks.description: Final sand of sealer coat(s) with 320-grit before clear topcoat. Creates glass-smooth surface for clear application.

quality_notes.all: Sand entire surface with 320 grit. Surface should feel glass-smooth. Do NOT sand through to stain.

tasks.name: Tack Clean Before Clear Coat
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust before first clear topcoat application. Any dust will be trapped in clear and visible.

quality_notes.all: Meticulous dust removal. Every particle trapped in clear coat is a visible defect.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Sand 320 → Tack → Ready for clear coat 1.

sop_modules.name: Clear Topcoat Application (Coat 1)
sop_modules.description: Apply first clear topcoat. Brush or spray per application_method_clear. Conditional: coating_type includes clear.

tasks.name: Clear Coat 1 — Brush
tasks.description: Apply first clear topcoat with brush. Thin, even coat with the grain. Tip once to level — do NOT overwork. Strain clear before pouring.

quality_notes.all: No drips, sags, holidays, or brush marks. Tip once with grain. Do NOT re-brush — marks will not level. Strain clear before pour.

tasks.name: Clear Coat 1 — Spray
tasks.description: Spray first clear topcoat. Consistent distance and speed for uniform mil thickness. HVLP preferred for clear coat.

quality_notes.all: No drips, sags, holidays, or orange peel. Uniform coverage. Proper mil thickness.

sop_modules.name: Clear Coat Interstage
sop_modules.description: Sand between clear coats and inspect. Conditional: clear_coats >= 2.

tasks.name: Sand Clear Coat (320-400 Grit)
tasks.description: Sand cured clear coat with 320 grit (QT3-QT4) or 400 grit (QT5). Level surface, remove dust nibs and imperfections.

quality_notes.QT3: Spot sand nibs and rough spots. 320 grit.
quality_notes.QT4: Full surface sand. 320 grit. Uniform scratch pattern.
quality_notes.QT5: Thorough full sand. 400 grit. Glass-smooth between coats.

tasks.name: Tack Clean Between Clear Coats
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust with tack cloth before next clear coat.

quality_notes.all: Meticulous dust removal. Dust in clear coat = visible trapped particles.

tasks.name: Inspect Clear Coat
tasks.description: Visual inspection of sanded clear coat before next coat. Check for dust nibs, runs, holidays, adhesion issues.

quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan at 3 feet — mark all visible defects
quality_notes.QT5: Critical inspection under raking light — zero tolerance

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Sand clear → Tack → Inspect → Apply next clear coat. Runs between each clear coat except the final one.

sop_modules.name: Clear Topcoat Application (Coat 2)
sop_modules.description: Apply second clear topcoat. Conditional: clear_coats >= 2.

tasks.name: Clear Coat 2
tasks.description: Apply second clear topcoat using same method as coat 1. Builds film thickness and depth.

quality_notes.all: Same technique as coat 1. Faster than coat 1 — consistent substrate. No application defects.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Applied after clear interstage. If clear_coats = 3, followed by another interstage + coat 3.

sop_modules.name: Clear Topcoat Application (Coat 3)
sop_modules.description: Apply third clear topcoat for maximum film build and depth. Conditional: clear_coats = 3.

tasks.name: Clear Coat 3
tasks.description: Apply third and final clear topcoat. Maximum film build. This is the finish surface — extra care for defect-free application.

quality_notes.QT5: Final surface coat — zero tolerance for defects. Perfect uniform sheen. No brush marks, no orange peel, no dust inclusions.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Final clear coat. Followed by MOD_TRST_CLEANUP.

sop_modules.name: Trim Stain/Clear Cleanup
sop_modules.description: Protection teardown, final inspection, touch-up, and tool cleanup.

tasks.name: Protection Teardown
tasks.description: Remove all protection materials — floor drops, wall masking, fixture covers. Remove tape carefully to avoid damaging fresh clear coat.

quality_notes.all: Remove tape carefully — pull at 45 degrees away from fresh clear coat to avoid lifting.

tasks.name: Vacuum Sanding Dust
tasks.description: Vacuum all sanding dust from floor, surfaces, and surrounding area. Stain/clear work generates significant dust from multiple sanding stages.

quality_notes.all: Thorough vacuum of entire work area. Sanding dust from 5+ grit levels accumulates.

tasks.name: Final Inspection
tasks.description: Final quality check of all stained/clear-coated trim surfaces. Verify color uniformity, sheen consistency, and defect-free finish.

quality_notes.QT3: Quick glance at 6 feet — no obvious defects, uniform stain color
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan at 3 feet — uniform color, consistent sheen, no visible defects
quality_notes.QT5: Critical inspection at arm's length under raking light — zero tolerance, uniform color and sheen across all surfaces

tasks.name: Touch-Up
tasks.description: Address remaining defects found during final inspection. Touch up with same clear product. Spot sand and recoat as needed.

quality_notes.QT4: Address all visible defects — blend touch-up into surrounding finish
quality_notes.QT5: Address every imperfection — may need full coat over repair areas to equalize sheen

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Remove masking → Vacuum → Final inspect → Touch-up → Clean tools.

round_configurations.name: QT3 Stain + Clear (2 Coats Total)
round_configurations.description: Budget: 1 stain + 0 sealer + 1 clear = 2 total coats.
round_configurations.notes: Minimal coat stack. Stain + dry verify + clear. No sealer. No clear interstage.

round_configurations.name: QT4 Stain + Sealer + Clear (4 Coats Total)
round_configurations.description: Standard: 1 stain + 1 sealer + 2 clear = 4 total coats.
round_configurations.notes: Professional standard. Stain + dry + sealer + sealer sand + clear 1 + interstage + clear 2.

round_configurations.name: QT5 Stain + 2 Sealer + 3 Clear (6 Coats Total)
round_configurations.description: Premium: 1 stain + 2 sealer + 3 clear = 6 total coats.
round_configurations.notes: Maximum film build. 6 total coats with interstage sanding between each.

round_configurations.name: Stain Only (1-2 Coats)
round_configurations.description: Stain only — no sealer or clear coat.
round_configurations.notes: Minimal workflow. Stain + wipe only. No interstage.

assumptions.value: All stain application methods include a wipe step — wipe time is built into the stain application rate, not a separate task
assumptions.note: Wipe is integral to stain application — not separable. Rate includes apply + dwell + wipe.

assumptions.value: Sealer uses same application method as clear coat (application_method_clear drives both sealer and clear)
assumptions.note: Sealer and clear are same coating type (film-forming). Same method makes sense.
